definitions.definition: Gravitation is the universal attractive interaction between any two masses.
The gravitational force between two masses acts along the line joining their centres and is always attractive.
G is the universal constant appearing in Newton's law of universal gravitation.
A force whose direction is along the line joining the particle to a fixed centre. Gravitational force is a central force.
Every planet moves in an elliptical orbit with the Sun at one focus of the ellipse.
The line joining a planet to the Sun sweeps out equal areas in equal intervals of time.
For planets orbiting the same central body, the square of the orbital period is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis.
The point in a planet's elliptical orbit closest to the Sun.
The point in a planet's elliptical orbit farthest from the Sun.
Half of the major axis of an elliptical orbit; denoted by a.
The acceleration acquired by a freely falling body due to gravitational attraction.

definitions.term: Acceleration Due to Gravity at Height
definitions.definition: At height h above Earth's surface, the distance from Earth's centre is R+h, so g decreases with height.
When h is much smaller than Earth's radius, the first-order approximation gives the decrease of g with height.

definitions.term: Acceleration Due to Gravity at Depth
definitions.definition: For a uniform Earth, acceleration due to gravity decreases linearly with depth below the surface.
Gravitational potential at a point is the gravitational potential energy per unit mass placed at that point.
The gravitational potential energy of a mass m at distance r from a spherical source mass M, taking zero energy at infinity, is negative.
In the standard gravitation convention, gravitational potential and potential energy are taken as zero when the separation tends to infinity.
The minimum initial speed required for an object to escape from a celestial body and reach infinity with zero final speed, neglecting atmosphere and other bodies.
The speed required for a satellite to maintain a circular orbit of radius r around a central mass M.
A body that revolves around a larger celestial body under gravitational influence.
The time taken by a satellite or planet to complete one revolution around its central body.
A satellite that appears stationary relative to an observer on Earth because its orbital motion matches Earth's rotation.
conditions: Orbit lies in the equatorial plane
Orbital period equals Earth's rotation period
Angular speed equals Earth's angular speed

definitions.definition: For a satellite in a circular orbit, total mechanical energy is negative, showing that the satellite is gravitationally bound.

laws_and_principles.name: Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation
laws_and_principles.statement: Every two masses attract each other with a force directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centres.
laws_and_principles.explanation: The force is attractive and acts along the line joining the centres.

laws_and_principles.name: Kepler's First Law — Law of Orbits
laws_and_principles.statement: Every planet moves in an elliptical orbit with the Sun at one focus.
laws_and_principles.explanation: The orbit is an ellipse; a circle is a special case of an ellipse.

laws_and_principles.name: Kepler's Second Law — Law of Areas
laws_and_principles.statement: The line joining a planet and the Sun sweeps equal areas in equal intervals of time.
laws_and_principles.explanation: The planet moves faster near perihelion and slower near aphelion.

laws_and_principles.name: Kepler's Third Law — Law of Periods
laws_and_principles.statement: The square of the orbital period is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis for bodies orbiting the same central mass.
laws_and_principles.explanation: A larger orbital size corresponds to a longer orbital period.

laws_and_principles.name: Variation of Acceleration Due to Gravity
laws_and_principles.statement: The value of g decreases with altitude and, for a uniform Earth, decreases with depth.
laws_and_principles.explanation: Increasing the distance from Earth's centre reduces gravitational acceleration.

golden_rules.title: Gravity is an inverse-square force
golden_rules.rule: For fixed masses, gravitational force varies as 1/r².
golden_rules.survival_tip: If separation doubles, gravitational force becomes one-fourth.

golden_rules.title: Kepler's area law means changing speed
golden_rules.rule: Equal areas are swept in equal times, so a planet moves faster when it is closer to the Sun and slower when it is farther away.
golden_rules.survival_tip: Fastest at perihelion; slowest at aphelion.

golden_rules.title: g decreases away from Earth's surface
golden_rules.rule: Acceleration due to gravity decreases with altitude and, for a uniform Earth, decreases linearly with depth.
golden_rules.survival_tip: At the centre of a uniform Earth, g becomes zero.

golden_rules.title: Potential is negative when zero is taken at infinity
golden_rules.rule: For an isolated mass, gravitational potential and gravitational potential energy are negative at finite distance.
golden_rules.survival_tip: As r increases, V becomes less negative and approaches zero.

golden_rules.title: Satellite speeds and energies follow orbit relations
golden_rules.rule: For a circular orbit, orbital speed decreases with radius, while total mechanical energy is negative.
golden_rules.survival_tip: Higher circular orbit → lower orbital speed but higher (less negative) total energy.

questions.explanation: Kepler's Second Law is the law of areas.

questions.question: The gravitational force between two masses varies with distance as:

questions.explanation: The distance from Earth's centre is R+h.

questions.explanation: Earth's escape velocity is approximately 11.2 km/s.

questions.question: For a circular satellite orbit, orbital speed is proportional to:

questions.explanation: A geostationary orbit is circular and lies in Earth's equatorial plane.

questions.question: For a uniform Earth, acceleration due to gravity at the centre is:
questions.explanation: For a uniform Earth, g decreases linearly with depth and becomes zero at the centre.

questions.question: According to Kepler's Third Law, for planets orbiting the same Sun:
questions.explanation: Kepler's Third Law gives T² ∝ a³.

questions.question: For a satellite in a circular orbit, the total mechanical energy is:
questions.explanation: E = −GMm/(2r), so the satellite is gravitationally bound.
